A.text: In a hydrogen atom the electron makes a transition from (n + 1)th level to the nth level. If n>>1, the frequency of radiation emitted is proportional to:
A.sol_text:
In hydrogen atom,

E_n = -E_0/n^2

Where E_0 is Ionisation Energy of H.

For transition from (n + 1) to n, the energy of emitted radiation is equal to the difference in energies of levels.

ΔE = E_(n+1) - E_n

ΔE = E_0(1/n^2 + 1/(n+1)^2)

ΔE = hν = E_0((n+1)^2 - n^2)/(n^2(n+1)^2)

hν = E_0(2n + 1)/(n^4(1 + 1/n)^2)

hν = E_0(n(2 + 1/n))/(n^4(1 + 1/n)^2)

Since n >> 1

Hence, 1/n ≈ 0

hν = E_0[2/n^3]

ν ∝ 1/n^3

A.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
A.text: In the following digital circuit, what will be the output at 'Z', when the input (A, B) are (1,0), (0,0), (1,1), (0,1) :
A.sol_text:
From the circuit diagram:

P = NAND(A, B) = A NAND B
Q = NAND(A, B) = A NAND B
R = NAND(P, Q)
Z = NAND(P, R)

Simplifying the logic:
P = A NAND B = (AB)'
Q = A NAND B = (AB)'
R = P NAND Q = (P.Q)' = ((AB)'.(AB)')' = (AB)' [since (X.X)' = X']

Z = P NAND R = (P.R)' = ((AB)'.(AB)')' = (AB)'

Alternatively, analyzing the circuit step by step:
The two NAND gates at top and bottom both take inputs A and B.
Their outputs P and Q feed into another NAND gate producing R.
R and P feed into the final NAND gate producing Z.

Z = (P + R)' = P'R' (By De Morgan's law applied to NAND)

Simplifying through Boolean algebra:
Z = (AB)' (after complete reduction)

Truth table for Z = (AB)':
When A=1, B=0: AB=0, so Z=(0)'=1
When A=0, B=0: AB=0, so Z=(0)'=1
When A=1, B=1: AB=1, so Z=(1)'=0
When A=0, B=1: AB=0, so Z=(0)'=1

Therefore: Z = 1, 1, 0, 1

Wait, checking against options: This gives 1,1,0,1 which is option (4).

Re-examining the circuit more carefully from the provided solution:
The final expression derived is Z = AB

Truth table for Z = AB:
When A=1, B=0: Z = 1.0 = 0
When A=0, B=0: Z = 0.0 = 0
When A=1, B=1: Z = 1.1 = 1
When A=0, B=1: Z = 0.1 = 0

Therefore: Z = 0, 0, 1, 0

A.text: The height 'h' at which the weight of a body will be the same as that at the same depth 'h' from the surface of the earth is (Radius of the earth is R and effect of the rotation of the earth is neglected):

Weight of body is same at P and Q

g_P = g_Q

GM_1 / (R - h)^2 = GM / (R + h)^2

A.subject: Physics
A.text: An ideal gas in a closed container is slowly heated. As its temperature increases, which of the following statements are true ?
A.sol_text:
The mean free path of molecules of an ideal gas is given as:
lambda = V / (sqrt(2) * pi * d^2 * N)

where: V = Volume of container
N = No of molecules

Hence with increasing temp since volume of container does not change (closed container), so mean free path is unchanged.

Average collision time = mean free path / V_av = lambda / (avg speed of molecules)

since: avg speed proportional to sqrt(T)

therefore: Avg coll. time proportional to 1/sqrt(T)

Hence with increase in temperature the average collision time decreases.

Therefore the correct statements are:
(C) the mean free path remains unchanged
(D) the mean collision time remains unchanged

Wait, reviewing the solution: The mean free path remains unchanged because V and N are constant in a closed container. The mean collision time decreases because while the mean free path is constant, the average speed of molecules increases with temperature (v_avg proportional to sqrt(T)), so collision time = lambda/v_avg decreases.

Actually, statement (D) says mean collision time remains unchanged - this is FALSE.
Statement (C) says mean free path remains unchanged - this is TRUE.

Statement (B) says mean collision time decreases - this is TRUE.

So statements (B) and (C) are true.

A.text: A charge Q is distributed over two concentric conducting thin spherical shells radii r and R (R > r). If the surface charge densities on the two shells are equal, the electric potential at the common centre is:

Since charge density sigma is same for both spheres, so
sigma = Q_1/(4π r^2) = Q_2/(4π R^2) => Q_1/Q_2 = r^2/R^2

Q_1 + Q_2 = Q => Q_2 * r^2/R^2 + Q_2 = Q

=> Q_2 = QR^2/(r^2 + R^2)

Q_1 = (r^2/R^2) * (R^2/(r^2 + R^2)) * Q = Qr^2/(R^2 + r^2)

Potential at centre 'O' = kQ_1/r + kQ_2/R

= k[Qr^2/(r(R^2 + r^2)) + QR^2/(R(R^2 + r^2))]

= kQ(r + R)/(R^2 + r^2) = 1/(4π epsilon_0) * (R + r)Q/(R^2 + r^2)

A.text: Two uniform circular discs are rotating independently in the same direction around their common axis passing through their centres. The moment of inertia and angular velocity of the first disc are 0.1 kg-m^2 and 10 rad s^(-1) respectively while those for the second one are 0.2 kg-m^2 and 5 rad s^(-1) respectively. At some instant they get stuck together and start rotating as a single system about their common axis with some angular speed. The Kinetic energy of the combined system is:

• Angular momentum conserved for the system

⇒ (1/2)(I_1 + I_2)omega_f^2
= (1/2)(0.1 + 0.2).(20/3)^2
= (0.3/2) × (400/9)
= (120/18)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A small point mass carrying some positive charge on it, is released from the edge of a table. There is a uniform electric field in this region in the horizontal direction. Which of the following options then correctly describe the trajectory of the mass? (Curves are drawn schematically and are not to scale).
options: Curve (1): Starting high on y-axis, curving downward and to the right
Curve (2): Starting at origin, curving upward and to the right
Curve (3): Starting at origin, curving upward and to the right
Curve (4): Straight line starting at origin going upward and to the right
A.sol_text:
At the initial position (edge of table), u = 0 (initial velocity is zero).

Forces acting on the particle:
1. Gravitational force: mg (downward, in -y direction)
2. Electric force: qE (horizontal, in +x direction)

Net force: F_net = sqrt((qE)^2 + (mg)^2)

Since the particle starts from rest (u = 0) and experiences a constant net force, the acceleration a will be constant in magnitude and direction.

Using Newton's second law:
a = F_net/m = constant

Since initial velocity is zero and acceleration is constant, the particle will travel in a straight line along the direction of the net force.

The direction of motion is determined by the vector sum of qE (horizontal) and mg (downward), which gives a straight line path at an angle to both axes.

This straight line path passes through the origin (starting point) and goes in the direction of the net acceleration, which is downward and to the right at some angle.

Therefore, the trajectory is a straight line, which corresponds to option (4).

A.text: When the temperature of a metal wire is increased from 0°C to 10°C, its length increases by 0.02%. The percentage change in its mass density will be closest to:
A.sol_text:
Given: ΔL/L = 0.02%

∴ ΔL = L α ΔT ⟹ ΔL/L = α ΔT = 0.02%

∴ β = 2α (Areal coefficient of expansion)
⟹ β ΔT = 2α ΔT = 0.04%

Volume = Area × Length

Density(ρ) = Mass/Volume = Mass/(Area × Length) = M/(AL)

⟹ Δρ/ρ = ΔM/M - ΔA/A - ΔL/L (Mass remains constant)

⟹ (Δρ/ρ) = ΔA/A + ΔL/L = β ΔT + α ΔT

= 0.04% + 0.02% = 0.06%

A.text: In a plane electromagnetic wave, the directions of electric field and magnetic field are represented by k and 2i - 2j, respectively. What is the unit vector along direction of propagation of the wave.
A.sol_text:

Direction of wave propagation = C = E × B

C = k × [(1/sqrt(2))(i - j)]

C = (1/sqrt(2))(k × i - k × j)

C = (1/sqrt(2))(i + j)

B.text: A light ray enters a solid glass sphere of refractive index μ = sqrt(3) at an angle of incidence 60°. The ray is both reflected and refracted at the farther surface of the sphere. The angle (in degrees) between the reflected and refracted rays at this surface is ____.

B.text: A particle of mass m is moving along the x-axis with initial velocity ui. It collides elastically with a particle of mass 10 m at rest and then moves with half its initial kinetic energy (see figure). If sin(theta_1) = sqrt(n) sin(theta_2), then value of n is ______.
B.sol_text:
By momentum conservation along y:
m*u1*sin(theta_1) = m2*u2*sin(theta_2)
i.e. m*u1*sin(theta_1) = 10*m*u2*sin(theta_2)
=> u1*sin(theta_1) = 10*u2*sin(theta_2) ...(i)

kf_m = (1/2)*ki_m
i.e. (1/2)*m*u1^2 = (1/2) * (1/2)*m*u^2
i.e. u1 = u/sqrt(2) ...(ii)

Also collision is elastic: k_i = k_f
(1/2)*m*u^2 = (1/2)*m*u1^2 + (1/2)*10*m*u2^2
(1/2)*m*u^2 = (1/2)*m*u1^2 + (1/2)*10*m*u2^2
(1/2)*m*u^2 = (1/2) * (1/2)*m*u^2 + (1/2)*10*m*u2^2
(1/4)*m*u^2 = (1/2)*10*m*u2^2

u2 = u/sqrt(20) ...(iii)

Putting (ii) & (iii) in (i):
(u/sqrt(2))*sin(theta_1) = 10*(u/sqrt(20))*sin(theta_2)

sin(theta_1) = sqrt(10)*sin(theta_2) => Hence n = 10
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.text: A square shaped hole of side l = a/2 is carved out at a distance d = a/2 from the centre 'O' of a uniform circular disk of radius a. If the distance of the centre of mass of the remaining portion from O is -9/x, value of X (to the nearest integer) is ____.
B.sol_text:
Using the principle of superposition, the center of mass of the remaining portion can be found using:

X_com = (m1*x1 - m2*x2)/(m1 - m2)

where:
- m1 = mass of complete disc
- m2 = removed mass (square hole)
- Let σ = surface mass density of disc material

m1 = σ*π*a^2
m2 = σ*(a/2)^2 = σ*a^2/4

The square hole is at distance d = a/2 from O.

With respect to 'O':
X_com = (σ*π*a^2*(0) - σ*(a^2/4)*(a/2)) / (σ*π*a^2 - σ*a^2/4)

X_com = (-σ*a^3/8) / (σ*a^2*(π - 1/4))

X_com = (-a/8) / (π - 1/4)

X_com = (-a/8) / ((4π - 1)/4)

X_com = (-a/8) * (4/(4π - 1))

X_com = -a/(2(4π - 1))

X_com = -a/(8π - 2)

Given that the distance is -9/x, we have:
-a/(2(4π - 1)) = -9/x

Therefore:
X = 2(4π - 1) = 2(4π - 1) = 8π - 2 = 8(3.14159...) - 2 ≈ 25.13 - 2 = 23.13

So, X = 2(4π - 1) = (8π - 2) = 23.12

Therefore, nearest integer value of X = 23
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The major product of the following reaction is: Starting material is a benzene ring with CH3, OH, and NO2 groups attached, reacted with conc. HNO3 + conc. H2SO4
options: Benzene ring with H3C, O2N, and NO2 groups (two NO2 groups ortho to each other, one meta to CH3)
Benzene ring with H3C, OH, NO2, and NO2 groups (OH and two NO2 groups)
Benzene ring with H3C, OH, and NO2 groups (single NO2 addition para to OH)
Benzene ring with H3C, OH, NO2, and NO2 groups (OH ortho, two NO2 groups)
A.sol_text:
The starting material is 4-methyl-2-nitrophenol (or similar isomer with CH3, OH, and NO2 on benzene ring).

When subjected to nitration with conc. HNO3 and conc. H2SO4:

1) Both OH and CH3 are electron-donating groups (activating groups), while NO2 is an electron-withdrawing group (deactivating group).

2) The OH group is a stronger activating group (ortho/para director) compared to CH3 (also ortho/para director).

3) The NO2 group is a deactivating group and meta-director.

4) Directing effects analysis:
   - OH directs incoming NO2 to ortho and para positions
   - CH3 directs incoming NO2 to ortho and para positions
   - NO2 directs incoming NO2 to meta position

5) In the given starting material structure, the most activated position is the one that is:
   - Ortho or para to OH (strong activator)
   - Ortho or para to CH3 (moderate activator)
   - Meta to existing NO2 (avoids deactivator)

6) The major product forms when the new NO2 group enters at the position ortho to OH (the strongest activating group) and para to CH3, which gives option (3).

7) The solution diagram shows that with more donating groups available, nitration occurs at the position activated by OH, giving the major product with a single additional NO2 group para to the existing substituents, while a minor product forms due to steric crowding when trying to add at alternative positions.

A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: Arrange the following labelled hydrogens in decreasing order of acidity: A structure showing a benzene ring fused with a cyclohexene ring. The benzene ring has NO2 at one position and OH (labelled d) at another position ortho to NO2. The cyclohexene ring has a triple bond C≡C-H (labelled Ha) at one position and a COOH group (with H labelled Hb) at another position. There is also an OH group (labelled Hc) on the cyclohexene ring.
A.sol_text:
Acidic strength order:
R-C(=O)-OH > R-OH > R-C≡C-H

Reason:
R-C(=O)-O^- is stable by equivalent resonance.

For carboxylic acid (Hb): COOH group is most acidic due to resonance stabilization of the conjugate base.

For phenolic OH (Hd): The OH attached to benzene ring with NO2 (electron-withdrawing group) ortho to it would be acidic, but NO2 is ortho to this position, making it moderately acidic.

For aliphatic OH (Hc): The OH on the saturated cyclohexene ring (aliphatic alcohol) is weakly acidic.

Two compounds A and B with same molecular formula (C3H6O) undergo Grignard's reaction with methylmagnesium bromide to give products C and D. Products C and D show following chemical tests.

Ceric ammonium nitrate Test: C - Positive, D - Positive
Lucas Test: C - Turbidity obtained after five minutes, D - Turbidity obtained immediately
Iodoform Test: C - Positive, D - Negative

C and D respectively are:
A.sol_text:
Given: Two compounds A and B with molecular formula C3H6O undergo Grignard's reaction with methylmagnesium bromide to give products C and D.

Analyzing the chemical tests:

1) Ceric ammonium nitrate Test (CAN test for alcohols): Both C and D are positive
   - This indicates both C and D contain alcohol (-OH) groups

2) Lucas Test: 
   - C shows turbidity after five minutes (slower reaction)
   - D shows turbidity immediately (faster reaction)
   - Lucas test rate: Primary alcohol (slow) < Secondary alcohol (faster) < Tertiary alcohol (immediate)
   - Therefore: C is a secondary alcohol, D is a tertiary alcohol

3) Iodoform Test:
   - C is positive (gives iodoform precipitate)
   - D is negative (no iodoform precipitate)
   - Iodoform test is positive for compounds having CH3-CH(OH)- or CH3-CO- group
   - Therefore: C must have CH3-CH(OH)- group, D does not have this structure

Since both A and B are C3H6O and react with CH3MgBr to form alcohols:
A and B must be aldehydes or ketones (C3H6O)

Possible structures for A and B:
- Propanal: CH3CH2CHO
- Propionaldehyde derivative
- Acetone: CH3COCH3
- Allyl aldehyde: H2C=CH-CHO

For product C (secondary alcohol with iodoform test positive):
Reactant A must be: H2C=CH-CHO (acrolein/allyl aldehyde)
Product C after Grignard reaction: H2C=CH-CH(OH)-CH3 (secondary alcohol with CH3-CH(OH)- group)

For product D (tertiary alcohol with iodoform test negative):
Reactant B must be: CH3-CO-CH3 (acetone)
Product D after Grignard reaction: CH3-C(-OH)(-CH3)-CH3 (tertiary alcohol)

Therefore:
C = H2C=CH-CH(-OH)-CH3
D = H3C-C(-OH)(-CH3)-CH3

Verification:
- C is secondary alcohol (Lucas test: 5 minutes) ✓
- D is tertiary alcohol (Lucas test: immediate) ✓
- C has CH3-CH(OH)- group (Iodoform test: positive) ✓
- D does not have CH3-CH(OH)- or CH3-CO- (Iodoform test: negative) ✓

A.text: The major product obtained from E2-elimination of 3-bromo-2-fluoropentane is:
options: CH3CH2-CH-CH=CH2 with Br above the first CH
CH3-CH2-C=CH-CH3 with Br above the C
CH3-CH=CH-CH-CH3 with F above the CH
CH3CH2CH=C-F with CH3 below the C
A.sol_text:
The substrate is 3-bromo-2-fluoropentane: CH3-CH2-CH(Br)-CH(F)-CH3

In E2 elimination, we need to identify the better leaving group and the most acidic H atoms.

Br is a better leaving group compared to F.

The H atoms on the carbon bearing Br (carbon 3) are more acidic than H atoms on the carbon bearing F (carbon 2) due to the electronegativity effect.

For E2 mechanism to proceed, we need H and leaving group (Br) on adjacent carbons in anti-periplanar geometry.

The Br is on carbon 3. The adjacent carbons are carbon 2 (bearing F) and carbon 4 (bearing CH3).

Carbon 2 has the more acidic H atoms (due to F being electronegative and withdrawing electron density, making the adjacent H more acidic).

When H is removed from carbon 2 and Br leaves from carbon 3, we form a double bond between carbons 2 and 3.

This gives: CH3-CH2-CH=C(F)-CH3

Alternatively written as: CH3CH2CH=C-F with CH3 attached to the sp2 carbon.

This is the most stable alkene having 5 alpha H atoms on the resulting structure, making it the major product.

The answer is option (4).

A.text: Consider the reaction sequence given below: t-BuBr + OH^⊖ in H2O → t-BuOH + Br^⊖ ......(1) with rate = k[t-BuBr]. t-BuBr + OH^⊖ in C2H5OH → alkene with CH3 groups + HOH + Br^⊖ ......(2) with rate = k[t-BuBr][OH^⊖]. Which of the following statements is true: (1) Changing the concentration of base will have no effect on reaction (1). (2) Changing the concentration of base will have no effect on reaction (2). (3) Changing the base from OH^⊖ to OR^⊖ will have no effect on reaction (2). (4) Doubling the concentration of base will double the rate of both the reactions.
options: Changing the concentration of base will have no effect on reaction (1)
Changing the concentration of base will have no effect on reaction (2)
Changing the base from OH^⊖ to OR^⊖ will have no effect on reaction (2)
Doubling the concentration of base will double the rate of both the reactions
A.sol_text: Reaction 1: SN1 mechanism. Rate = k[t-BuBr]. SN1 is independent of concentration of nucleophile/base. Therefore, changing the concentration of base will have no effect on reaction (1). This makes statement (1) TRUE. Reaction 2: E2 mechanism. Rate = k[t-BuBr][OH^⊖]. This is dependent on the concentration of base. Therefore, changing the concentration of base will affect reaction (2), making statement (2) FALSE. For statement (3): In E2 reactions, the nature of the base affects reactivity. Changing from OH^⊖ to OR^⊖ (where R is a bulky alkyl group) would change the steric effects and reactivity, so statement (3) is FALSE. For statement (4): Doubling [base] would double the rate of reaction (2) but would NOT affect reaction (1) since it is zero-order in base, making statement (4) FALSE. Therefore, only statement (1) is true.

A.text: The size of a raw mango shrinks to a much smaller size when kept in a concentrated salt solution. Which one of the following processes can explain this?
A.sol_text: Raw mango shrink in salt solution due to net transfer of water molecules from mango to salt solution due to phenomenon of osmosis. When a raw mango (which contains water and has lower salt concentration) is kept in a concentrated salt solution (which has higher salt concentration), water molecules move out of the mango cells into the salt solution through the cell membrane. This movement of solvent (water) molecules across a semipermeable membrane from a region of lower solute concentration to a region of higher solute concentration is called osmosis. As water leaves the mango cells, the mango shrinks in size. This process is also called plasmolysis when it occurs in plant cells.

A.text: The equation of the normal to the curve y = (1 + x)^(2y) + cos^2(sin^(-1) x) at x = 0 is:
A.sol_text:
Given equation of curve
y = (1 + x)^(2y) + cos^2(sin^(-1) x)
at x = 0
y = (1 + 0)^(2y) + cos^2(sin^(-1) 0)
y = 1 + 1
y = 2

So we have to find the normal at (0, 2)

Now, y = e^(2y ln(1+x)) + cos^2(cos^(-1) sqrt(1 - x^2))
y = e^(2y ln(1+x)) + (sqrt(1 - x^2))^2
y = e^(2y ln(1+x)) + (1 - x^2) .....(1)

Now differentiate w.r.t. x
y' = e^(2y ln(1+x)) [2y·(1/(1+x)) + ln(1+x)·2y'] - 2x

Put x = 0 & y = 2
y' = e^(2·2·ln(1)) [2·2·(1/(1+0)) + ln(1+0)·2y'] - 2·0
y' = e^0[4 + 0] - 0
y' = 4 = slope of tangent to the curve

so slope of normal to the curve = -1/4 {m1·m2 = -1}

Hence equation of normal at (0, 2) is
y - 2 = -1/4 (x - 0)
⇒ 4y - 8 = -x
⇒ x + 4y = 8

A.text: For some theta in (0, pi/2), if the eccentricity of the hyperbola x^2 - y^2*sec^2(theta) = 10 is sqrt(5) times the eccentricity of the ellipse x^2*sec^2(theta) + y^2 = 5, then the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse is:
A.sol_text:
Given theta in (0, pi/2)

equation of hyperbola => x^2 - y^2*sec^2(theta) = 10
=> x^2/10 - y^2/(10*cos^2(theta)) = 1

Hence eccentricity of hyperbola
(e_h) = sqrt(1 + (10*cos^2(theta))/10) = sqrt(1 + cos^2(theta)) ...(1)

where for hyperbola: e = sqrt(1 + b^2/a^2)

Now equation of ellipse => x^2*sec^2(theta) + y^2 = 5
=> x^2/(5*cos^2(theta)) + y^2/5 = 1

where for ellipse: e = sqrt(1 - a^2/b^2)

Hence eccentricity of ellipse
(e_E) = sqrt(1 - 5*cos^2(theta)/5) = sqrt(1 - cos^2(theta)) = |sin(theta)| = sin(theta) ...(2)

since theta in (0, pi/2)

given => e_h = sqrt(5)*e_E

=> sqrt(1 + cos^2(theta)) = sqrt(5)*sin(theta)

Squaring both sides:
1 + cos^2(theta) = 5*sin^2(theta)
1 + cos^2(theta) = 5(1 - cos^2(theta))
1 + cos^2(theta) = 5 - 5*cos^2(theta)
6*cos^2(theta) = 4

cos^2(theta) = 2/3 ...(3)

Now length of latus rectum of ellipse = 2a^2/b = 10*cos^2(theta)/sqrt(5) = 20/(3*sqrt(5)) = (4*sqrt(5))/3

A.text: Let E^C denote the complement of an event E. Let E₁, E₂ and E₃ be any pairwise independent events with P(E₁) > 0 and P(E₁ ∩ E₂ ∩ E₃) = 0. Then P(E₂^C ∩ E₃^C / E₁) is equal to:
A.sol_text:
Given E₁, E₂, E₃ are pairwise independent events
so P(E₁ ∩ E₂) = P(E₁).P(E₂)
and P(E₂ ∩ E₃) = P(E₂).P(E₃)
and P(E₃ ∩ E₁) = P(E₃).P(E₁)
& P(E₁ ∩ E₂ ∩ E₃) = 0

Now P(E₂^C ∩ E₃^C / E₁) = P[E₁ ∩ (E₂^C ∩ E₃^C)] / P(E₁)

= P(E₁) - [P(E₁ ∩ E₂) + P(E₁ ∩ E₃) - P(E₁ ∩ E₂ ∩ E₃)] / P(E₁)

= [P(E₁) - P(E₁).P(E₂) - P(E₁)P(E₃) - 0] / P(E₁)

= 1 - P(E₂) - P(E₃)

= [1 - P(E₃) - P(E₂)]

= P(E₃^C) - P(E₂)

A.text: If a curve y = f(x), passing through the point (1, 2), is the solution of the differential equation 2x^2 dy = (2xy + y^2)dx, then f(1/2) is equal to:

=> dy/dx = (2xy + y^2)/(2x^2) {Homogeneous D.E.}

Let y = xt
=> dy/dx = t + x(dt/dx)

=> t + x(dt/dx) = (2x·xt + x^2t^2)/(2x^2)

=> t + x(dt/dx) = t + t^2/2

=> x(dt/dx) = t^2/2

=> 2∫(dt/t^2) = ∫(dx/x)

=> 2(-1/t) = ln(x) + C

=> -2x/y = ln(x) + C {Put t = y/x}

Put x = 1 & y = 2:
then we get C = -1

=> -2x/y = ln(x) - 1

=> y = 2x/(1 - ln(x))

=> f(x) = 2x/(1 - log_e x)

So, f(1/2) = 2(1/2)/(1 - log_e(1/2)) = 1/(1 - (log_e 1 - log_e 2)) = 1/(1 - (0 - log_e 2)) = 1/(1 + log_e 2)
